Notes: CPU percent is process CPU divided by actual phase wall time, normalized to one core; no division by logical processors.
Memory is the median of endpoint-filtered periodic samples; eligible phase aggregates summarize per-trial metrics and paired deltas.

Last-GC heap, commit and fragmentation describe the most recent GC snapshot, not current live-object size; absent snapshots remain null. The non-GC private commit residual is an estimate, not a native allocation census.
Warmup, startup and explicit refresh duration are excluded from idle comparison.
Visible phase averages can include window-show or refresh settling work. Inspect the saved sample time distribution before treating a short full-phase CPU average as sustained steady activity.
Recorder counters describe intentional feature work; missing baseline fields remain null and never decide pair eligibility.
An unchanged-phase save may drain pending asynchronous work; repeated saves and failures are diagnostics to inspect, not proof of a defect.
Checkout SHA and measured production assembly SHA are different identities. Local paths and host/user names are omitted.
Short sequential synthetic batches do not establish installed-app absolute usage, causal statistical significance or long-session leak behavior.
